business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of PC and Console Video Games via Digital Stores

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 27 January 2009, entered into force 15 April 2010)
Convention between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (1990, as amended by Protocol of 2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 951.0), as amended; Ordinance on the Prevention of Money Laundering (AMLO, SR 955.01); Federal Act on Financial Services (FinSA, SR 950.1); Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220, Articles 621-685 concerning share capital, shareholders and corporate governance); Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411); Federal Act on the Swissness in the Indication of Origin (SR 232.112).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of existence and good standing for each corporate incorporator or ultimate beneficial owner entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial register or competent corporate registry in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin country is a party to the 1961 Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization at the Swiss Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of residential address for each proposed director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public, passport issuing authority, or recognised issuing authority in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn translation into German, French, or Italian if applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from a regulated financial institution for each founding shareholder and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank, being a prudentially regulated financial intermediary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with notarised signature of the bank officer

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial deed of incorporation including the Articles of Association (Statuten) and foundation audit report, if any
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary public competent for the canton of registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization within the Swiss juridical area; no apostille required for domestic Swiss documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, executive officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) consolidated sanctions list, the OFAC SDN list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, and the Swiss FIU watchlists. Politically exposed persons, including family members and close associates, are subject to enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and approval at senior management level. UBO identification is mandatory for any individual owning or controlling more than 25% of shares or voting rights.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix (Zentraler Firmenindex) and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be in Latin script. It may be expressed in German, French, Italian, Romansh, or a foreign-language term, provided the name is not misleading and does not create a likelihood of confusion with an existing registered name. Non-Latin scripts or substantial foreign transliterations require conversion into one of the Swiss official languages for definitive registration. Names containing 'Swiss', 'Suisse', 'Helvetia', or equivalent indications are permitted only where the undertaking satisfies the Swissness requirements of SR 232.112.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a formal name clearance rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the competent cantonal commercial register supervisory authority within 10 days of service of the rejection decision. A further appeal may be lodged with the Federal Administrative Court within 30 days of service. The preliminary clearance does not confer a vested right to the name, and final protection arises only upon registration in the commercial register.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not generally acceptable for the registered seat of a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft. The registered office must be a real, physically accessible location where corporate records, board minutes, and statutory books are available for inspection. A mere post office box or shared virtual address without actual personnel and infrastructure does not satisfy the commercial substance requirement and raises AML red flags.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated at 15-25% for a low-risk standard video game publishing AG without a statutory licence; the likelihood increases to 30-40% if the company engages in payment processing, open banking services, or cryptocurrency Web3 settlement functionalities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff based on share capital and document length

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Swiss law firm or corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark rate for Swiss fiduciary due diligence packages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss cantonal authorities, Swiss embassy or consulate, and sworn translators
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular fee schedule plus market translation fee

Registered office address and administrative support for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate services provider in the canton of registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for physical office, mail handling, and registered agent services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory scale based on paid-in share capital

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR) arts. 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft), in particular arts. 626-628 (statutes), 632 (share capital), 635 (paid-up capital), 640 (registration), 712r (mandatory board resolution); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung) arts. 13-21.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung der Gründung), statutes (Statuten), foundation report, and board acceptance declarations filed via the Swiss Commercial Register electronic portal (Simpli / e-GR).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000, divided into registered shares of nominal value at least CHF 0.01 each; at least CHF 50,000 must be paid up before registration. Cash contributions must be deposited into a Swiss bank blocked account (Sperrkonto) and the bank confirmation must be submitted to the notary and registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [Insert Company Name] AG. Adopted by unanimous written resolution of the first board of directors on [date]. 1. Subscription and payment of the share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 100,000 registered shares of CHF 1.00 each, are ratified; the blocked-account deposit of CHF 50,000 made by the founders is accepted. 2. The registered office is fixed at [address], [municipality], Switzerland, and the Commercial Register is the competent public register. 3. [Name] is appointed Chair of the Board, [Name] is appointed Delegate and CEO, and [Name] is appointed financial reporting officer. Each appointment takes effect upon commercial registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug via the Swiss Commercial Register name search and reservation desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the proposed commercial name for admissibility check against existing registrations and the SIC (Swiss Industrial Classification). The name must be distinctive and truthful, must not mislead as to the corporate purpose, and must clearly indicate the legal form AG. Request a name reservation if the cantonal office offers a preliminary reservation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, file two alternative names promptly; otherwise amend the suffix or descriptive element and resubmit through the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss-bank in the Canton of Zug (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank) or a licensed bank recognized for Sperrkonto confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the company in formation, deposit the minimum paid-up capital of CHF 50,000, and obtain the bank's written confirmation that the amount is irrevocably credited and blocked until the Commercial Register entry. The confirmation must identify the deposit date, account holder, and amount.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further detail, provide enhanced source-of-wealth documentation or use a Swiss-resident professional introducer. Refunds are permissible only after the registry has refused or cancelled the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public with authority in the Canton of Zug (öffentliche Urkundsperson)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have the articles of incorporation and all founding resolutions notarially executed. The notary certifies the founder identities, the share capital structure, the paid-up capital confirmation, the election of the board, and the acceptance of office by each board member.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all founders and directors
Written acceptance of office by board members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any notarial requisitions or deficiencies noted by the notary. If a defect cannot be cured, the entire incorporation instrument must be re-executed before the same or another notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (electronic filing via e-GR / Simpli)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, statutes, board resolutions, officer acceptances, and the official registration application in the prescribed form. Verify the capital statement and legal-purpose declarations, pay the registration fee, and respond to the registry's formal review within the statutory deadline.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for the filing agent
Commercial register application form signed by authorized officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a formal query, file the requested supplements or clarifications within 10 calendar days. The registry will not enter the company while capital or name conditions remain unsatisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette and Legal Effectiveness
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Commercial Register enters the company, the SHAB publication is generated automatically. Confirm the published particulars (name, legal form, registered office, purpose, board members, and registered capital) and retrieve the official commercial register extract confirming legal personality.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If disclosure contains inaccuracies, file a corrected entry with the Commercial Register and request a rectified SHAB publication; otherwise the defect remains effective against third parties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration Zug; Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA); Swiss Social Insurance institutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, apply for the UID number and VAT registration if worldwide taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per year. Register for direct federal, cantonal, and municipal income taxes. If employees are hired, register with the relevant AHV/Social Security clearing house and workers' accident insurance (SUVA or private insurer).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authorities require additional information, file clarifications promptly. Missed VAT registration can be cured by submitting a late registration through ESTV with explanation and interest as applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — digital game publishing via Steam and PlayStation Store does not constitute an industrial establishment under the Swiss Labour Act (Arbeitsgesetz) and requires no cantonal industrial permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory operating license required. Steamworks distribution agreement with Valve Corporation and PlayStation Partner agreement, if any, are private commercial contracts and do not give rise to a public-law permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — not listed under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV/EIA-R); no physical installation, heavy emission source, or hazardous installation is established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial discharges or emissions. The operation produces no wastewater, process cooling water, VOCs, or hazardous waste. General municipal waste and electronic equipment disposal obligations under Swiss Environmental Protection Act apply to office operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable to digital-only premises. If office space is rented, the landlord must provide municipal fire-safety and building-code compliance for ordinary offices. If staff are employed, SUVA occupational-safety rules and accident insurance registration apply; no industrial structural-load or fire-engineering clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC). Official portal: estv.admin.ch (also eService and Swiss UID portal uid.admin.ch)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft obtains its federal company number (UID CHE-Nr.) through the commercial register procedure upon incorporation; this UID automatically serves as the VAT registration number for Swiss VAT purposes when required. Foreign entities (non-resident in Switzerland or Liechtenstein) with VAT-liable activities in Switzerland must appoint a Swiss VAT representative (domiciled in CH) and file a registration form each. Non-resident businesses without a Swiss permanent establishment are not subject to Swiss corporate income tax but must register for Swiss VAT if they generate taxable turnover in Switzerland exceeding the statutory threshold. Foreign agencies supplying digital services to Swiss private customers from abroad must register for Swiss VAT regardless of turnover, applying the simplified procedure for electronic services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Swiss AG is a corporate taxpayer; federal and cantonal/communal profit taxes apply at entity level; no pass-through)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box (Genossenschaftswahl) regime exists in Swiss tax law. Available elections: (1) Swiss VAT group election (Art. 15 VAT Act) granted to closely linked entities, (2) Swiss tax group election for federal and cantonal profit taxes under Art. 61 f. of the Federal Tax Harmonisation Act, allowing offsetting of results among Swiss group companies, (3) participation exemption is automatic for qualifying dividends/capital gains, with no formal election required. Hybrid mismatch elections under OECD BEPS are generally no longer available; Switzerland complies with ATAD principles.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / MWST / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide taxable turnover (Art. 10 VAT Act); non-resident suppliers of digital services, telecommunication and broadcasting services to Swiss private consumers must register regardless of threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC) or digital stamping regime as of 2024. E-invoicing is permitted if the recipient consents and the invoice is archived in an electronic form compliant with Art. 63 VAT Act (punctual and complete retention). The ESTV does not require API-based clearance for VAT documents. Swiss taxpayers are obliged to retain electronic records for 10 years and must provide them to authorities upon request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating for goods is available under Art. 23 VAT Act for direct exports of tangible goods; the exporter must hold proof of transport out of Switzerland. For digital services (electronically supplied games, download codes, software), the usual place of supply rule (Art. 7 VAT Act) places B2B and B2C supplies to customers outside Switzerland outside Swiss VAT, so effectively no Swiss VAT is chargeable; this is not an export zero-rating mechanism. For B2C supplies to Swiss consumers, the standard rate applies. Offshore services listed in Art. 23(3) VAT Act (e.g. services relating to foreign real estate) may be zero-rated if the recipient is abroad and the service is used abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (E-dec or NCTS document)
Transport document evidencing physical export (CMR waybill, bill of lading, air waybill or courier receipt)
Evidence of payment (bank statement, inward remittance certificate where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claiming export zero-rating without valid proof of export triggers VAT reassessment, default interest (5% per annum) and potential fine for tax evasion (up to 3× the tax evaded) or VAT fraud (up to 4× the tax evaded) under Art. 96–99 VAT Act. In addition, wilful violation of record-keeping duties is punishable with fines up to CHF 10,000; for a stock corporation the law targets the governing body representatives, and civil clawback options apply in case of deliberate misstatement. Swiss anti-fraud procedure permits retrospective reclassification of a supply, removal of the zero-rating benefit, and assessment of unpaid VAT for up to 10 years in tax evasion cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB - Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse, BNS)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility regime. CHF is freely convertible on both the current and capital account; there is no exchange control law and no foreign exchange administration permit is required for cross-border payments, profit remittance or dividend distribution. The only friction is the 35% anticipatory withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends distributed by a Swiss AG, which is fully or partially refundable under an applicable tax treaty or, for Swiss resident shareholders, via refund. There are no restrictions on holding foreign currency balances and no obligation to convert export revenues into CHF.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender rules. Switzerland guarantees free movement of capital under Article 27 para. 2 of the Federal Constitution. Export proceeds from digital publishing (Steam/PlayStation payouts) may be retained in USD/EUR, held onshore or offshore, and are not subject to any statutory repatriation timeline or mandatory conversion ratio. Only statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations to the SNB apply, without any conversion or confiscation mandate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Einzahlungskonto) for statutory share capital deposit
Operational Multi-Currency Account (CHF/EUR/USD) for treasury and platform payouts
Operational CHF Account with SEPA EUR corridor
Operational Cross-Border Account for royalty and collection flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium as auxiliary rails, Low as primary banking. Foreign EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, other non-Swiss licensed payment institutions) may be used as secondary treasury corridors, but they cannot replace a licensed Swiss bank for statutory capital deposits, payroll tax, VAT settlement, or a corporate account with full banking substance. A Swiss FINMA-regulated fintech/payment institution may hold client funds up to CHF 100 million under the fintech licence regime, but the CH_AG blueprint should anchor all platform payouts in a fully licensed Swiss banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Required in substance for corporate onboarding. Swiss AMLA and FINMA Circular 2020/1 require the bank to identify the legal entity, authorized signatories and ultimate beneficial owner. Most tier-1 Swiss banks demand a physical or video-based identification interview with at least one authorized director and the UBO. Remote opening is possible but discretionary, normally requiring qualified electronic signatures, apostilled corporate documents, and an approved compliance committee. For a Swiss AG with foreign beneficial owners and digital gaming revenue, an in-person meeting at the Swiss branch materially accelerates approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner combined with high-velocity, low-ticket digital gaming revenue credited from overseas platform operators (Valve Corporation for Steam, PlayStation Store)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled articles of association (Statuten), Swiss commercial register extract (Handelsregisterauszug), UBO declaration and passport copies, board minutes confirming Swiss substance, signed Steam/PlayStation publisher agreements, 12-month projected treasury forecast, and a notarized signature card to the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Royalty-heavy outbound flows to foreign developers perceived as intellectual property de-risking or tax-driven profit shifting
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany license agreements with arm's-length royalty rates, transfer pricing documentation, advance tax ruling from the cantonal tax administration, payroll and office substance evidence, board decision records, and audited financials proving real decision-making in Switzerland.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pejorative association with the 'Crypto Valley' Web3 narrative or any tokenised fan-engagement project linked to the publishing entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written legal opinion from Swiss counsel on FINMA token classification, confirmation of no payment/securities licence trigger, clear separation of fiat treasury from digital-asset wallets, no ICO/IDO activity, board resolution prohibiting unlicensed crypto services, and an AML compliance map per FINMA Guidance 02/2021.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fragmented micro-transaction economics: thousands of Steam/console revenue line items aggregated into monthly platform payouts that are difficult to reconcile with VAT and Swiss accounting records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform settlement reports from Valve and PlayStation with per-game granularity, daily revenue extracts, auditable P&L ledger trail, Swiss VAT registration evidence, tax audit correspondence, and a reconciliation certificate issued by a Swiss chartered accountant.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire protocol: SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 credit transfer from the foreign shareholder to the CH_AG bank using Swiss IBAN format (CH + two check digits + 5-digit bank code + 12-digit account number) and BIC/SWIFT. The remittance must state the company name, a purpose code such as COMC (Commercial Payment) or LIQU (Liquidity) for capital contribution, and a capital subscription reference. Verification requires the notarial deed of capital increase, Swiss commercial register extract, bank confirmation to the statutory auditor, and advance notification to the receiving bank. Funds derived from e-commerce platform receivables must not be mixed with statutory capital in a single suspicious wire.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 (gpi-tracked) for USD/EUR/CHF royalty, developer and distributor payments; SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant for EU counterparties using the Swiss IBAN; domestic CHF settlements via SIC/e-Finance rails operated by SIX. Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP 600) is permissible only for physical console hardware or merchandising where goods documentation exists, while digital licensing and royalty flows use open-account MT103 wires. Remittance must include ISO 20022 purpose codes ROYA (royalty) or LICF (licence fee); for treaty-benefited recipients, the Swiss paying bank may require the applicable withholding tax relief declaration (Form A) before settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards (CHF/EUR and CHF/USD) executed under ISDA 2002 with CSA at UBS or ZKB to lock USD Steam payouts
European FX options on major USD revenue tranches to retain upside while protecting the Swiss franc budget
Cross-currency swaps converting USD/EUR platform receivables into CHF for dividend readiness and Swiss VAT cash-flow planning

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are technically permissible for exotic pairs but unnecessary for CHF given full convertibility and liquid onshore forward markets; Swiss banks will reject CHF NDFs unless a genuine non-deliverability restriction is proven

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Federal, Cantonal, and Communal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (e.g., Zug Financial Authority) for the Confederation, Canton, and Commune
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; extension up to 12 months upon application
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 5% p.a. plus penalty surcharges up to 30% of assessed tax; persistent non-filing may trigger debt enforcement and eventual strike-off from the Commercial Register through bankruptcy proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), Swiss VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly: due 60 days after the end of each quarter; annual option available for taxpayers with turnover below CHF 100,000 (approx. USD 115,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to CHF 10,000, late-payment interest, and default penalties of 1–2% per annum; recurring failure may lead to FTA enforcement and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employer Wage Declaration for OASI/AVS and Social Security
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 March after the reporting calendar year (with possible extension)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines plus statutory interest on unpaid contributions; violation may lead to criminal prosecution under Swiss social security law and debt collection resulting in strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary (full) audit required if, for two consecutive fiscal years, two of the three thresholds are exceeded: total assets > CHF 20 million; total revenue > CHF 40 million; average headcount > 250 FTE. Limited audit required for smaller AGs; waiver permitted if < 10 FTE and unanimous shareholder consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) is the minimum; Swiss GAAP FER accepted; IFRS (or US GAAP) mandatory for listed entities. Digital game publishing revenue (Steam/console royalties) recognized in accordance with OR or IFRS 15 when applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss AGs must maintain an ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) register under Art. 697j OR and AMLA. No annual government filing is required; however, the board must annually verify and update the register, and all share transfers must be recorded immediately to ensure AML/due diligence accuracy. Shareholders' register and UBO data must be kept at the registered office and are subject to inspection by competent authorities.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 1,000 – 3,000 per year (approx. USD 1,100 – 3,300), depending on provider and canton
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CHF 3,000 – 10,000 per year (approx. USD 3,300 – 11,000), depending on company size and transaction complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax (assessed on after-tax profit, equivalent to approximately 7.83% of pre-tax profit), plus Zug cantonal and communal corporate income tax of approximately 4.0% to 4.5% of pre-tax profit, producing a combined effective total corporate income tax rate in canton Zug of approximately 11.8% to 12.2%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Switzerland grants no general tax holidays. Available reductions for an AG publishing PC/console games in Zug: licence (patent) box applying up to 90% relief to qualifying IP royalty income; 150% R&D super-deduction on eligible research and development labour costs; notional interest deduction on excess qualifying equity; participation relief on substantial dividend income; and capital tax abatements for qualifying participations and intangible assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual corporate tax return for legal entities ('Steuererklärung juristische Personen' — harmonized Form C/A issued by the Swiss Tax Conference), filed simultaneously with the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) and the Zug Canton Tax Office through the official e-filing portal ('SwissTax' / eTax on zg.ch).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The statutory deadline is six months after the close of the commercial financial year; the Zug tax authority routinely grants extension upon request, making the practical due date approximately eight months after year-end (around 30 September for a 31 December balance sheet date). The AG must also settle quarterly corporate tax prepayments during the assessment year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the tax period (Steuerperiode) and the full financial year covered; the audit year normally equals the calendar year unless the AG has a non-calendar commercial year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders have no filing obligation in Switzerland. The Swiss AG files in its own name and must enter the same fiscal year-end used in the statutory commercial accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company registration identifiers: Swiss UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), Swiss Commercial Register number, legal form and the seat in canton Zug.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The fields are pre-populated from the Commercial Register; a non-resident director with representative signature authority must verify that the UID is active and that the registered seat corresponds to the effective centre of administration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual net profit or loss according to the statutory commercial balance sheet (Jahresgewinn/Jahresverlust), before income tax expense, including capital gains from the divestment of game IP and platform store assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the profit prepared under Swiss GAAP (OR) or IFRS. For Steam/PlayStation digital publishing, record all Valve, Sony and console store royalties net of platform commissions as gross turnover, with a full reconciliation of platform payout statements annexed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying participation income (dividends, liquidation proceeds and capital gains on qualifying holdings) eligible for the Swiss participation relief deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The participation deduction is claimed at the AG level. Non-resident shareholders should not include Swiss dividends in their local filing but must instead pursue treaty reduction or refund of the 35% anticipatory tax imposed at the AG level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments to the book profit, including disallowed expenses, hidden profit distributions, the interest limitation rule (Art. 59a DBG) on shareholder loans, and arm's length transfer pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All intercompany royalty, licence and service fees paid to a foreign parent or group IP owner must be disclosed and supported by transfer pricing documentation attached to the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Segregation of privileged profits qualifying for the Zug licence (patent) box, including the 90% deduction on qualifying IP royalties derived from gaming software, patents and comparable digital rights.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The AG must attach the detailed patent box working papers and demonstrate in Switzerland the substantive R&D activity, qualified personnel and equipment required to justify the Zug patent box relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a procedural administrative fine (Ordnungsbusse) of up to CHF 10,000 under Art. 194 DBG; additionally, the AG owes late-payment interest at 3% p.a. on federal tax and approximately 5% p.a. on Zug cantonal tax. Understatement of taxable profit triggers an evasion surcharge of up to three times the federal tax evaded (Art. 175 DBG) and a parallel cantonal surcharge, while qualified tax fraud (Steuerbetrug) is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment of up to three years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss anticipatory tax (Verrechnungssteuer) must be withheld by the Swiss AG on all dividend distributions regardless of the shareholder's residence (Art. 4 VStG). The gross 35% rate applies at source; the shareholder can recover the excess through treaty relief and refund procedures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For treaty relief, the beneficial owner must obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its home tax administration and file a formal refund application with the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) within three years of the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was distributed, usually on Form 820/23; the TRC must confirm beneficial ownership and sufficient substantive presence in the treaty state. Where an advance determination or a genuine pre-approved structure exists, the AG may apply the reduced DTA rate at source; missing TRC or substance-denying shell structures cause denial of treaty benefits under Swiss anti-abuse doctrine.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: Switzerland imposes no anticipatory tax on pure IP royalties paid cross-border; most Swiss DTAs allocate sole taxing rights to the residence state of the beneficial owner (0% or 5% residual rates under older conventions). Interest: ordinary intercompany business interest is treaty-exempt and not subject to Swiss anticipatory tax; only Swiss bond-type debt instruments or structured pass-through interest bear 35% anticipatory tax, typically reduced to 0% to 10% under an applicable DTA. All royalty and interest payments must satisfy the arm's length standard of Art. 58 DBG to avoid recharacterization as hidden profit distributions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Master File and Local File compliant with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines (Chapter V, as endorsed by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration's circular of 2020/2021) are mandatory where annual consolidated group turnover exceeds CHF 50 million or where volume of cross-border controlled transactions exceeds CHF 10 million per category; below those thresholds, a proportionate contemporary TP record must still prove the arm's length nature of royalties, platform fees and profit allocations.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland is not covered by the Offshore Economic Substance Regulations applicable to the ESR-listed jurisdictions. However, Swiss law and treaty practice impose substance requirements that the AG must satisfy: genuine management and board activity, operating staff, premises and records in Switzerland. For digital Steam/console publishers claiming the Zug licence box or treaty benefits, the substance doctrine requires locally performed R&D, decision-making and commercial control. In addition, the OECD Pillar Two GloBE rules apply to multinational groups exceeding EUR 750 million consolidated turnover, and the Swiss qualified domestic minimum top-up tax came into force on 1 January 2025, effectively anchoring a 15% minimum effective tax rate for in-scope groups.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and tax fraud (Steuerhinterziehung / Steuerbetrug)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally or grossly negligently suppressing Steam, PlayStation Store and console platform revenue from the Swiss tax return, inflating deductions, maintaining unreported offshore royalty accounts, or signing false and misleading corporate tax declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal surcharge of up to three times the federal tax evaded (Art. 175 DBG); Zug cantonal surcharge of up to three times the evaded cantonal and communal tax; recovery of the evaded tax plus statutory interest; qualified evasion through false or forged documents constitutes Steuerbetrug punished under Art. 186 DBG by a monetary fine or imprisonment of up to three years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who prepare, approve or sign a false return are jointly and severally liable for the evaded taxes and surcharges; personal liability is asserted directly against board members, Swiss bank accounts may be attached, travel bans can be issued under Art. 91 SchKG, and criminal conviction may lead to disqualification from holding board office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and abuse of Domicile status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Zug 'mailbox AG' structure without real commercial substance: no Swiss-resident directors with actual management authority, no local employees, all Steam publishing decisions taken abroad, IP legal ownership held by a non-resident shell, and no coherent business records maintained at the registered seat.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of Zug licence box relief, denial of treaty benefits, retroactive full taxation of privileged profit at the combined Zug effective rate, reassessment of hidden profit distributions, and potential administrative liquidation under Art. 731b OR where the AG lacks a lawful organisation or effective seat; capital tax and interest surcharges follow the reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members who knowingly maintained a sham substance structure are personally liable for resulting tax deficiencies and damages; enforcement may proceed against personal assets, the directors may face prosecution for attempted evasion, and exit from Switzerland may be formally blocked.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing mismatching and incomplete documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging intercompany royalties, platform fee allocations, or residual profit splits with the foreign publishing headquarters that deviate from the arm's length result, computing no benchmark analysis, or failing to prepare and submit the Master File/Local File once the CHF 50 million group turnover threshold is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward profit adjustments by ESTV and Zug with qualified interest at 3%–5% p.a.; denial of royalty expense documentation; in aggravated cases of gross negligence an administrative penalty surcharge of up to 30% of the reallocated income; systematic non-compliance may trigger a formal transfer pricing audit with retroactive reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed declarations based on undocumented or fictitious transfer prices bear personal financial liability for the unpaid differential tax and interest; where fabricated comparability studies are produced, directors expose themselves to criminal sanctions for false records before Swiss tax and criminal authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends or constructive benefits (including advances, interest-free loans or IP transfers to foreign group companies) to a non-resident parent or treasury without withholding and remitting the statutory 35% anticipatory tax, or filing a false refund claim relying on a shell ownership chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the unremitted 35% anticipatory tax together with a penalty of up to the full amount of the withheld tax (Art. 175–177 VStG); interest accruals; intentional failure is criminally punishable by a fine or imprisonment of up to one year; refund claims are irrevocably barred where the statutory three-year filing period is missed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members and responsible tax officers are strictly and severally liable for unremitted anticipatory tax; collection proceedings extend directly to their personal Swiss bank accounts and real estate, travel bans may be imposed on the managing directors, and in aggravated crypto/treasury diversion cases, prosecution follows under Art. 14 VStrR and the Swiss Criminal Code.
